BiblicalUsage: A grape — the fruit of the vine. Joseph's fellow prisoner dreams of a vine whose clusters bring forth ripe grapes in Genesis 40:10, the traveller may eat grapes his fill in his neighbour's vineyard in Deuteronomy 23:24, and Amos promises a day when the mountains drop sweet wine in Amos 9:13. But Hosea warns that Israel loves flagons of wine while looking to other gods in Hosea 3:1.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the grape shows how God turns small fruit into joy — wine for gladness, harvest for hope — and how the same gift can be twisted into idolatry. I hold that every good gift is meant to point me back to the Giver, and the day Amos promises, when the hills melt with sweet wine, is worth waiting for.
